spatial_claims.claim: Points lie in order A, D, E, C along line AC (D between A and E, E between D and C)
AB and AC meet at common endpoint A forming angle BAC; triangle ABC is formed by joining BC
DF drawn through D parallel to BC meets AB at F (F lies on segment AB)
EG drawn through E parallel to BC meets AB at G (G lies on segment AB)
DF is parallel to EG (both parallel to BC)
D lies on side AE of triangle AEG
F lies on side AG of triangle AEG
DF is parallel to base EG of triangle AEG, cutting sides proportionally
E lies on side AC of triangle ABC
G lies on side AB of triangle ABC
EG is parallel to base BC of triangle ABC, cutting sides proportionally

configuration_map: Triangle ABC with vertex A. On side AC, points in order A, D, E, C. Through D, a line parallel to BC meets AB at F. Through E, a line parallel to BC meets AB at G. On side AB, the resulting order is A, F, G, B. Sub-triangle AEG contains point D on side AE and point F on side AG with DF parallel to base EG. The full triangle ABC contains point E on side AC and point G on side AB with EG parallel to base BC. All point positions are consistent with the parallel line constructions and the ordering constraints.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. The configuration is a standard triangle with two interior parallel lines to BC. Points F and G on AB correspond properly to D and E on AC. Applications of Proposition 6.2 correctly identify valid sub-triangles (AEG and ABC) with parallel lines cutting their sides, and the points used are verified to lie on the appropriate sides. The remaining steps (6, 8-12) are purely algebraic proportion manipulations with no spatial content.
